title: Special bit vanishes under the special-bit-false conditioning
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and take the hard distribution on samples, conditioned first on the event that Alice's and Bob's input sets are disjoint and then further conditioned on the event that Bob's special bit $y_T$ is false. Under this doubly-conditioned distribution, Bob's special bit $y_T$ equals $\mathtt{false}$ almost surely.
hypotheses_covered: measure is the disjoint-conditioned hard distribution further conditioned on the special bit being false
replaced: Under $D ∧ Y_{T}=false$, Bob's special bit is almost surely \texttt{false}.
